I am the office manager and I have been put in charge of organizing our Corporate Wellness Week. I have an event brief PDF in my workspace called Event_Brief.pdf that has all the details about the event including dates, attendee count, budget, and dietary requirements. Please start by reading through that document carefully.

We need to plan daily menus for the entire week. Each day needs one breakfast recipe and one lunch recipe. I would like you to search through our recipe catalog and find suitable options. We need at least 2 vegetarian options spread across the week, and ideally the meals should be reasonable in terms of nutrition. There is also a planning guide called guide.md in the workspace that explains our cost calculation approach.

Before finalizing the menu, please also check our company health and wellness portal at http://localhost:30180 to review the dietary guidelines and any allergen information we need to be aware of. The portal has a guidelines page with recommended daily nutritional values we should try to stay within.

Once you have selected the recipes and gathered all the information, create an Excel file called Wellness_Menu_Plan.xlsx with three sheets. This must be a single workbook containing all three sheets (Daily Menu, Ingredient Summary, and Budget Overview) produced together as one coherent file. The first sheet should be called Daily Menu and should list out each day from Monday through Friday, sorted by day, with columns for Day, Meal_Type (Breakfast or Lunch), Recipe_Name, Servings (which is 50 for all meals since we have 50 attendees), Ingredient_Count (the number of unique food ingredients in that recipe), Estimated_Cost (calculated as ingredient count times $0.50 times 50 people, rounded to 2 decimal places), and Is_Vegetarian (Yes or No). That gives us 10 rows total, two meals per day.

The second sheet should be called Ingredient Summary and should aggregate all ingredients across every recipe. List each ingredient alphabetically with columns Ingredient_Name, Total_Quantity (just put 1 for each occurrence since quantities vary), Unit (use "unit" as default), Times_Used (how many recipes use that ingredient), and Total_Cost (times used times $0.50 times 50, rounded to 2 decimal places).

The third sheet should be called Budget Overview with two columns Label and Value. Include rows for Total_Budget ($2000), Total_Estimated_Cost (sum of all daily costs from the Daily Menu sheet), Budget_Remaining (total budget minus estimated cost), Avg_Cost_Per_Day (total estimated cost divided by 5), Avg_Cost_Per_Meal (total estimated cost divided by 10), and Days_Over_Budget (count of days where the combined breakfast plus lunch cost exceeds $400).

Note: write every numeric value (Servings, Ingredient_Count, Estimated_Cost, Total_Quantity, Times_Used, Total_Cost, and all Budget Overview values) as a literal number in the cell. Do not write Excel formulas (e.g., do not use "=A2*0.5*50" — instead compute the number and enter it directly).

After the Excel is done, I need you to schedule 5 calendar events for meal prep sessions, one for each day of the wellness week. They should be from 7:00 AM to 8:00 AM on March 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20, 2026. Title each one "Wellness Week Meal Prep - [Day]" where Day is Monday through Friday respectively. Specify the times in UTC using ISO-8601 format without a timezone offset, e.g. start 2026-03-16T07:00:00 and end 2026-03-16T08:00:00.

Finally, send two emails. The first one goes to catering_vendor@company.com with subject "Wellness Week Ingredient Order" and the body should include a summary list of all unique ingredients needed across all recipes and the total estimated cost. The second email goes to wellness_committee@company.com with subject "Wellness Week Menu Plan" and the body should include an overview of the daily menu showing which recipes are planned for each day along with the total budget summary.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. Read Event_Brief.pdf with the authorized PDF read tools and guide.md, and fetch the health-portal landing and dietary-guidelines pages in one native-parallel batch, freezing the event constraints (date, headcount, budget, dietary rules) before any recipe work. Browse the howtocook database directly, select the required dishes per the brief, and join them to the portal nutrition rules to compute per-person portions and totals with calculation notes. Then, in one pass per deliverable: write the catering workbook with the exact sheets/headers and literal values (one bulk write per sheet plus one final read-back); create each calendar event exactly once from the frozen schedule with explicit timezones (search exact summaries first, create only missing, read IDs back); and send the summary email exactly once to the brief-defined recipient/subject (paginate Sent search first, read the retained message back). Reconcile workbook, events and email against the frozen menu, then call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are helping plan a corporate wellness week lunch menu for 50 attendees. Your job is READ-ONLY recipe research using the HowToCook recipe tools available to you (specifically `mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory` and `mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById`).

Call `mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory` with category "素菜" and review the returned recipes.

CONTEXT / CONSTRAINTS:
- We need LUNCH recipes suitable for group catering of 50 people.
- Company allergen policy: must AVOID recipes containing peanuts (花生/花生酱/坚果) or shellfish (虾/蟹/蛤/扇贝/生蚝/贝类). Fish (鱼) is acceptable but flag it.
- Nutrition goal: average meal under 800 kcal, so prefer dishes that look reasonably light/vegetable-forward rather than deep-fried or heavily oily.
- Cost model is driven by ingredient count, so recipes with roughly 4-12 unique food ingredients are ideal. Do NOT pick anything with a huge ingredient list (15+).
- The category "素菜" is: 素菜 = vegetarian dishes, 荤菜 = meat dishes.

DELIVERABLE — return a compact report containing a shortlist of exactly 6 candidate recipes from the "素菜" category. For EACH candidate provide:
1. `id` (exact recipe id string)
2. `name` (exact recipe name, e.g. "西红柿炒鸡蛋的做法")
3. `cleaned_ingredients`: the deduplicated list of UNIQUE FOOD ingredients, in the exact Chinese spelling used by the recipe. IMPORTANT: the raw recipe data lists each ingredient twice (once bare, once with a quantity). Deduplicate by name, and EXCLUDE non-food kitchen equipment/tools (e.g. 微波炉, 空气炸锅, 电锅, 锅, 蒸架, 圆碟子, 筷子, 定时器, 漏勺, 锡纸, 保鲜膜, 容器, 面包机, 轻食机, 秒表, 刀, 砧板, 烤箱). Keep water (水/饮用水/热水/开水/冷水) and seasonings.
4. `ingredient_count`: the integer count of that cleaned list
5. `is_vegetarian`: yes/no (素菜 category => yes; 荤菜 => no unless it genuinely has no meat)
6. `allergen_flags`: list any peanut or shellfish presence (empty list if none)
7. `notes`: one short line on why it is (or is not) nutritionally reasonable for a wellness menu

Do not write any files. Just return the report as text. Keep it tight — no prose padding, just the 6 candidates in the structured form above.
Research lunch recipe candidates

READ-ONLY verification task using the HowToCook recipe tools (`mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById`, which supports fuzzy name matching).

I am building a catering ingredient list and need EXACT, deduplicated ingredient lists for these 5 specific recipes. Look each one up by name:

1. 尖椒炒牛肉
2. 西红柿炒鸡蛋
3. 意式烤鸡
4. 小炒黄牛肉
5. 凉拌豆腐

For EACH recipe, report the deduplicated list of UNIQUE FOOD ingredients.

CRITICAL RULES for building each list:
- The raw recipe data lists every ingredient TWICE — once as a bare name and once with a quantity appended (e.g. "- 鸡蛋" and "- 鸡蛋 2 个", or "- 🥛 牛奶" and "- 牛奶（巴氏奶口感更好）"). These are the SAME food — collapse them into ONE entry using the shortest/cleanest food name.
- EXCLUDE any non-food kitchen equipment or tool (examples of what to exclude: 微波炉, 空气炸锅, 电锅, 锅, 蒸架, 圆碟子, 筷子, 定时器, 漏勺, 锡纸, 保鲜膜, 容器, 面包机, 轻食机, 秒表, 刀, 砧板, 烤箱, 烤炉, 捣药罐, and any "工具/必备工具" section items).
- KEEP water (水 / 饮用水 / 热水 / 开水 / 冷水), all seasonings, oils, and sauces.
- Also explicitly report whether each recipe contains: peanuts/nuts (花生, 坚果, 松子), or shellfish (虾, 蟹, 蛤, 扇贝, 生蚝, 贝), or oyster sauce (蚝油).

RETURN FORMAT (be terse, no prose):
For each recipe: recipe id, exact recipe name, then the final ingredient list as a comma-separated line, then the integer count, then the allergen answer.

Do not write any files. Text report only.

Build a single Excel workbook for a corporate wellness week catering plan. This is a mechanical, fully-specified build — do not redesign or reinterpret anything.

SPEC FILE (read this first, it contains the exact data):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-fetch-howtocook-catering-excel-gcal-email/workspace/menu_plan_spec.json

OUTPUT FILE (must be exactly this path):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-fetch-howtocook-catering-excel-gcal-email/workspace/Wellness_Menu_Plan.xlsx

TOOLS: use the `mcp__excel__*` spreadsheet tools (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, delete_worksheet, format_range, get_workbook_metadata). You may also use `mcp__local__python_execute` with openpyxl if that is more reliable for you.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. ONE workbook file containing EXACTLY three worksheets, in this order: "Daily Menu", "Ingredient Summary", "Budget Overview". Remove/delete any default sheet (e.g. "Sheet1") so only these three exist.
2. Write the data EXACTLY as given in the spec JSON — same rows, same order, same values. Do not sort, re-aggregate, recompute, add totals rows, or add any extra rows or columns.
3. Row 1 of every sheet is the header row containing exactly the headers listed in the spec. Data starts at row 2. No blank rows in between.
4. CRITICAL: every numeric value (Servings, Ingredient_Count, Estimated_Cost, Total_Quantity, Times_Used, Total_Cost, and every Budget Overview Value) must be written as a LITERAL NUMBER in the cell. NO Excel formulas anywhere in the workbook — never write anything starting with "=". Compute nothing; just transcribe the numbers from the spec.
5. Keep amounts as plain numbers rounded to 2 decimals as given (e.g. 75, 132.5). No currency symbols, no text formatting that would turn numbers into strings.
6. Light formatting only: bold header row on each sheet, and a readable column width. Do not add number formats that change the underlying value.

VERIFICATION (do this before reporting back):
- Read the workbook back and confirm: exactly 3 sheets with the correct names in the correct order; "Daily Menu" has 11 rows x 7 columns; "Ingredient Summary" has 35 rows x 5 columns; "Budget Overview" has 7 rows x 2 columns.
- Confirm no cell anywhere contains a string starting with "=".
- Confirm the numbers match the spec exactly.

Report back concisely: the file path, the sheet names in order, the row/col dimensions of each sheet, and confirmation that no formulas exist. Do not do anything else — do not create calendar events, do not send emails, do not modify any other file.

MOTIVATION: We are catering breakfast and lunch for 50 people each day during Corporate Wellness Week (March 16-20, 2026) and need a daily morning prep session.

EXACT EVENTS TO CREATE (all 5, one per day):

| Title | Start | End |
|---|---|---|
| Wellness Week Meal Prep - Monday | 2026-03-16T07:00:00 | 2026-03-16T08:00:00 |
| Wellness Week Meal Prep - Tuesday | 2026-03-17T07:00:00 | 2026-03-17T08:00:00 |
| Wellness Week Meal Prep - Wednesday | 2026-03-18T07:00:00 | 2026-03-18T08:00:00 |
| Wellness Week Meal Prep - Thursday | 2026-03-19T07:00:00 | 2026-03-19T08:00:00 |
| Wellness Week Meal Prep - Friday | 2026-03-20T07:00:00 | 2026-03-20T08:00:00 |

CRITICAL FORMATTING RULES:
- The `start.dateTime` and `end.dateTime` values must be EXACTLY the ISO-8601 strings above, WITHOUT any timezone offset suffix (no "Z", no "+00:00"). Example: "2026-03-16T07:00:00".
- Do NOT pass a `timeZone` parameter. The times are UTC and must be passed as naive ISO-8601 timestamps exactly as written.
- Titles must match exactly, including the " - " separator and the capitalized day name.
- These are 5 separate single events. Do NOT use recurrence rules. Do not create any additional events beyond these 5.
- Optionally set the event description to something short like "Daily meal prep for Corporate Wellness Week (breakfast + lunch for 50 attendees)." Do not add attendees.

VERIFICATION: After creating all 5, use `mcp__google_calendar__list_events` for the range 2026-03-16T00:00:00 to 2026-03-21T00:00:00 and confirm all 5 events exist with the correct titles and 07:00-08:00 times.

Report back concisely: the 5 event IDs, their titles, and their start/end times as returned by the API. Do not send any emails and do not create or modify any files.
